26.speaker: Narrator
26.text: I heard a knock on the door.

29.speaker: Narrator
29.text: He slowly made his way towards the chair in front of my desk and sat down.

30.speaker: Deivid Wisci
30.text: "First of all, thank you for your time."

33.speaker: Player
33.text: "Please make it quick. I have other business to attend to."

34.speaker: Deivid Wisci
34.text: "Of course. I will be as fast as I can."

35.speaker: Deivid Wisci
35.text: "I wanted to ask you how you are doing."

39.speaker: Deivid Wisci
39.text: "It looks like war is truly upon us."

40.speaker: Deivid Wisci
40.text: "It must be taking a toll on you, just like it did on me all those years ago."

41.speaker: Deivid Wisci
41.text: "But of course, I won't presume to understand what you are going through right now."

42.speaker: Deivid Wisci
42.text: "I was never the leader of a nation during wartime, after all."

44.speaker: Player
44.text: "I am only interested in the results of this war. Nothing more."

45.speaker: Player
45.text: "Honestly. I am tired, Deivid. I am tired of it all."

46.speaker: Deivid Wisci
46.text: "Please, be sure to take some time for yourself."

47.speaker: Deivid Wisci
47.text: "Oh, I know the feeling. Trust me. I know."

48.speaker: Deivid Wisci
48.text: "Sometimes you just want to throw away all the responsibility and escape."

49.speaker: Deivid Wisci
49.text: "Perhaps into the wilderness, perhaps to the sea."

51.speaker: Deivid Wisci
51.text: "If you ignore the mental fatigue, it will slowly creep in on you. It will poison your thoughts."

52.speaker: Deivid Wisci
52.text: "Please be sure to take some time for yourself amid all this."

53.speaker: Deivid Wisci
53.text: "If you ignore the mental fatigue, it will slowly creep in on you. It will poison your thoughts."

54.speaker: Player
54.text: "I'm not in the mood for lectures."

56.speaker: Deivid Wisci
56.text: "Don't mind me. I'm just an old man getting ahead of himself."

57.speaker: Deivid Wisci
57.text: "Thank you for taking my advice over the years."

58.speaker: Deivid Wisci
58.text: "Don't mind me. I'm just an old man getting ahead of himself."

59.speaker: Deivid Wisci
59.text: "Thank you for taking my advice over the years."

60.speaker: Player
60.text: "I'm not in the mood for lectures."

62.speaker: Player
62.text: "That would be nice, wouldn't it? But I could never do that."

63.speaker: Player
63.text: "Yes. Exactly. That is what I want to do. I want to get away from this office."

64.speaker: Deivid Wisci
64.text: "It is good to fantasize, but unfortunately, men of power like yourself are bound by duty and their responsibility to the nation."

65.speaker: Deivid Wisci
65.text: "Unfortunately, men of power are bound by duty and their responsibility to the nation."

67.speaker: Deivid Wisci
67.text: "It has been many years since you were in my classroom."

72.speaker: Deivid Wisci
72.text: "I had the chance to watch my student grow into a fine and strong leader in my lifetime. What a privilege indeed."

73.speaker: Deivid Wisci
73.text: "You have brought reform to Sordland. You, my student, actually did it."

77.speaker: Deivid Wisci
77.text: "You don't know how proud I was to be alongside you."

78.speaker: Deivid Wisci
78.text: "You tried your best to bring reform to Sordland. That is valiant in itself."

79.speaker: Deivid Wisci
79.text: "It is okay to feel frustrated by failure. But change unfortunately doesn't happen easily."

80.speaker: Deivid Wisci
80.text: "You paved a path for future generations to follow, and they will remember you for it."

81.speaker: Deivid Wisci
81.text: "If there is one thing I learned from you, it is that power changes people."

82.speaker: Deivid Wisci
82.text: "It makes them do things that were not imaginable before."

83.speaker: Player
83.text: "I hope you are not trying to take a stab at me right now, Deivid."

84.speaker: Deivid Wisci
84.text: "It's just a simple observation. Don't pay heed to this old man."

85.speaker: Player
85.text: "True. But it changed me for better."

86.speaker: Deivid Wisci
86.text: "Perhaps. But it also takes its toll."

88.speaker: Deivid Wisci
88.text: "That is correct. But sometimes the ends do not justify the means."

89.speaker: Player
89.text: "This was only the beginning. Much more awaits on the horizon."

90.speaker: Player
90.text: "I still can't believe that we did it."

93.speaker: Deivid Wisci
93.text: "You actually managed to make me jump for joy. At my age!"

94.speaker: Deivid Wisci
94.text: "I know my student. I know you. You have the capability to do so much more."

95.speaker: Deivid Wisci
95.text: "That's the spirit! We can't be sulking about our failures for too long. Otherwise we will spiral into despair."

96.speaker: Player
96.text: "That's right. I will do whatever I can to leave a good world for the ones who will come after us."

97.speaker: Player
97.text: "When all is said and done, we still have failed."

98.speaker: Deivid Wisci
98.text: "That is the reality, yes. But, we can't be sulking about our failures for too long. Otherwise we will spiral into despair."

101.speaker: Deivid Wisci
101.text: "This country does not need any more despair."

103.speaker: Deivid Wisci
103.text: "How are you feeling about your chances?"

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: Deivid coughed again. This time, for longer.

106.speaker: Player
106.text: "I can't say for sure, but I'm hopeful."

108.speaker: Deivid Wisci
108.text: "Good. That is what a leader should say."

110.speaker: Deivid Wisci
110.text: "I'm afraid I have an announcement to make to you."

114.speaker: Deivid Wisci
114.text: "After the term is done, I will be retiring."

115.speaker: Player
115.text: "I would be lying if I said I wasn't expecting this."

117.speaker: Player
117.text: "Deivid. I can't accept this. You're irreplaceable in my cabinet."

118.speaker: Deivid Wisci
118.text: "I have been in this line of work for many decades now."

119.speaker: Deivid Wisci
119.text: "I swore an oath to myself years ago."

120.speaker: Deivid Wisci
120.text: "I would quit if I ever felt like I didn't have the physical capability to serve anymore. At that point, I would become a hindrance."

122.speaker: Deivid Wisci
122.text: "My bones are aching, my hands are shaking, my voice is failing."

123.speaker: Deivid Wisci
123.text: "Besides, I am sure you can find a younger minister who is a little more full of life."

124.speaker: Narrator
124.text: He winked at me and chuckled which turned into another cough.

125.speaker: Player
125.text: "I see. Thank you for letting me know."

126.speaker: Player
126.text: "You have been a mentor, a teacher and a friend. Thank you for your service to this country."

153.text: "Before I go, I want to mention something."

154.speaker: Narrator
154.text: He looked around before grabbing my arm and lowering his voice.

155.speaker: Deivid Wisci
155.text: "Be careful of the military. I think they are planning something."

156.speaker: Deivid Wisci
156.text: "I have lived long enough to see two coups in my lifetime, and let's just say I have gotten better at recognizing the signs."

157.speaker: Deivid Wisci
157.text: "You must remember what happened to my father Anton. Just be careful and take care of your family."

158.speaker: Deivid Wisci
158.text: "Take this as the last piece of advice from me."

159.speaker: Narrator
159.text: He suddenly raised his voice again.

160.speaker: Deivid Wisci
160.text: "We are probably being watched so I must be very brief."
